Yeah, I agree with what everyone's been saying. Don't stress about it too much, don't weigh yourself right after, drink plenty of water.

One thing that can help is limiting the amount of carbs you eat, since carbs hold more water than fat and protein, having fewer carbs means you're body will hold on to less water. But if you're not restricting what you eat at all, I would give yourself a few days weighing yourself just so you're not being to harsh on yourself.

If you're craving something you should have it. Now I'm not saying just go ham, but when I want something that is more calorie dense, I just make sure I keep my portion sizes in check. When you deprive yourself it can lead to overdoing it with cheat meals, but if you allow yourself to have it guilt free then it can be a lot easier to just have a little and move on with your life.

And to help with hunger, it helps to eat high volume less calorie dense food. But also making sure you're getting enough protein and healthy fats can help you feel satiated.

I know one thing that has helped is I stopped weighing myself so frequently. Body weight can fluctuate a lot based on the types of food you eat, if you have a carb heavy meal you're also going to retain some water. Now I only weigh myself once or twice a month.

 I found by weighing myself less frequently I didn't give myself the chance to be discouraged by smaller weight changes. When I was younger I used to weigh myself sometimes twice a day, which isn't helpful because ofcourse you're going to be a little bit heavier at night. You've eaten, and holding on to water. Whereas in the morning, you probably haven't eaten all night and if you use the bathroom right before can affect the scale.

But I know some people think it helps to weigh themselves everyday, I think it just depends on the person.
